translationRepairs: On bingchen Tang Rui, adjutant of the Tianxiong Army, was made Remonstrance Counsellor; Zhao Tong, chief secretary, became Remending Officer; and Song Lingxun, chief military aide from the Emperor's original entourage, was made prefect of Cizhou.

On bingchen Tang Rui, adjutant of the Tianxiong Army, was made Remonstrance Counsellor; Zhao Tuan, chief secretary, became Gentleman of the Imperial Diary; and Song Lingxun, chief military aide from the Emperor's original entourage, was made prefect of Cizhou.
趙彖 is Zhao Tuan, not Zhao Tong; 起居郎 is the court diarist, not a 'Remending Officer'.

On bingchen Tianxiong Army adjutant Tang Rui was made Remonstrance Counsellor; chief secretary Zhao Tong was made Remending Officer; original follower chief military aide Song Lingxun was made Cizhou prefect.

On bingchen Tianxiong Army adjutant Tang Rui was made Remonstrance Counsellor; chief secretary Zhao Tuan was made Gentleman of the Imperial Diary; original follower chief military aide Song Lingxun was made Cizhou prefect.
Same errors as the idiomatic field: 彖 is Tuan and 起居郎 is the imperial diarist.

On dingchou Cui Jujian, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Director of the Secretariat; Zhang Jizuo, former prefect of Cai, was made General of the Left Martial Guard and appointed deputy commissioner for imperial tomb bridges, roads, and relay stations.

On dingchou Cui Jujian, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Director of the Palace Library; Zhang Jizuo, former prefect of Cai, was made General of the Left Martial Guard and appointed deputy commissioner for imperial tomb bridges, roads, and relay stations.
秘書監 is the Palace Library director, not the Secretariat; the same chapter later renders 秘書監 as Director of the Palace Library.

On dingchou Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Jujian was made Director of the Secretariat; former Cai Prefecture prefect Zhang Jizuo was made General of the Left Martial Guard and appointed deputy commissioner for imperial tomb bridges, roads, and relay stations.

On dingchou Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Jujian was made Director of the Palace Library; former Cai Prefecture prefect Zhang Jizuo was made General of the Left Martial Guard and appointed deputy commissioner for imperial tomb bridges, roads, and relay stations.
Same mistranslation of 秘書監 as Secretariat rather than Palace Library.

On wuyin he took the Hall of Bright Hall with guards and escort as prescribed, palace music was played, and the ministers in court dress took their places. An edict proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the fifth year of Changxing to the first year of Yingshun.

On wuyin he took the Mingtang Hall with guards and escort as prescribed, palace music was played, and the ministers in court dress took their places. An edict proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the fifth year of Changxing to the first year of Yingshun.
明堂殿 is the Mingtang (Bright Hall); 'Hall of Bright Hall' doubles the building word.

On wuyin he took the Hall of Bright Hall; guards and escort followed the rite, palace suspended music was played, the ministers took their places in court dress, and an edict proclaimed a general amnesty for all under heaven, changing the fifth year of Changxing to the first year of Yingshun.

On wuyin he took the Mingtang Hall; guards and escort followed the rite, palace suspended music was played, the ministers took their places in court dress, and an edict proclaimed a general amnesty for all under heaven, changing the fifth year of Changxing to the first year of Yingshun.
Same doubled rendering of 明堂殿.
Huangfu Li, former training commissioner of Mingzhou, was advanced honorary Grand Guardian and made commissioner of Yanzhou;
Huangfu Li, former training commissioner of Mingzhou, was advanced honorary Grand Guardian and made commissioner of Fuzhou;
鄜州 is Fuzhou, not Yanzhou; 鄜 is a different graph and place from 兗/延/岩.
Former Mingzhou training commissioner Huangfu Li was advanced honorary Grand Guardian and appointed Yanzhou military commissioner;
Former Mingzhou training commissioner Huangfu Li was advanced honorary Grand Guardian and appointed Fuzhou military commissioner;
Same mistranslation of 鄜州 as Yanzhou.
Cui Wan, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat drafter, was made Vice Minister of Works while continuing his former duties.
Cui Zhuo, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat drafter, was made Vice Minister of Works while continuing his former duties.
崔棁 is Cui Zhuo (or Tuo); Wan does not match 棁.
Hanlin Academician and Secretariat drafter Cui Wan was made Vice Minister of Works, continuing in his former duties.
Hanlin Academician and Secretariat drafter Cui Zhuo was made Vice Minister of Works, continuing in his former duties.
Same romanization error for 崔棁.

Meng Hanqiong, Palace Attendant of the Southern Bureau, General of Agile Cavalry, General of the Left Guard, and director of the Palace Domestic Service, was advanced Grand Preceptor with the Opening of a Prefecture and Three Departments of Equal Standing and granted the merit title Loyal Integrity, Upholding the Dynasty, and Preserving Tranquility.

Meng Hanqiong, Palace Attendant of the Southern Bureau, General of Agile Cavalry, General of the Left Guard, and director of the Palace Domestic Service, was advanced to Unequaled in Honor (kaifu yitong sansi) and granted the merit title Loyal Integrity, Upholding the Dynasty, and Preserving Tranquility.
開府儀同三司 is the honor Unequaled in Honor, not a Grand Preceptor title (太師).
On xinyou Fan Zheng, former envoy of Yanzhou, was made Director of the Palace Workshops.
On xinyou Fan Zheng, former envoy of Yunzhou, was made Director of the Palace Workshops.
鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou; 鄆 and 兗/延 are different prefectures.
On xinyou former Yanzhou envoy Fan Zheng was made Director of the Palace Workshops.
On xinyou former Yunzhou envoy Fan Zheng was made Director of the Palace Workshops.
Same mistranslation of 鄆州 as Yanzhou.
On jiachen of the third month Wei Rene, former Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was made its minister.
On jiachen of the third month Wei Ren'e, former Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was made its minister.
魏仁鍔 is Wei Ren'e; 鍔 is è, not a silent final e on Rene.
Third month jiachen: former Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Wei Rene was made Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
Third month jiachen: former Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Wei Ren'e was made Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
Same romanization error for 魏仁鍔.

That night the Emperor rode out through Xuanyuan Gate with a hundred horsemen and said to Murong Qian, commander of the Crane-Control Guard, "If you truly have horses, let the Crane-Control follow me."
That night the Emperor rode out through Xuanwu Gate with a hundred horsemen and said to Murong Qian, commander of the Crane-Control Guard, "If you truly have horses, let the Crane-Control follow me."
元武門 is the Xuanwu Gate (玄武, with 玄 written 元); Xuanyuan is 軒轅, a different name.
That night the Emperor rode out through Xuanyuan Gate with a hundred horsemen and said to Crane-Control commander Murong Qian: "If you truly have horses, let the Crane-Control follow me."
That night the Emperor rode out through Xuanwu Gate with a hundred horsemen and said to Crane-Control commander Murong Qian: "If you truly have horses, let the Crane-Control follow me."
Same mistranslation of 元武門 as Xuanyuan Gate.
Jingtang said, "Wang Hongzan of Weizhou is an old acquaintance who knows how affairs are managed. Let us first go to Hongzan and devise a plan."
Jingtang said, "Wang Hongzhi of Weizhou is an old acquaintance who knows how affairs are managed. Let us first go to Hongzhi and devise a plan."
王宏贄 is Wang Hongzhi; 贄 is zhì, not zan.
He dispatched Hongzan's son, Palace Guard Wang Luan, to Weizhou; by then Hongzan had already escorted the Emperor to the prefectural offices.
He dispatched Hongzhi's son, Dianzhi Wang Luan, to Weizhou; by then Hongzhi had already escorted the Emperor to the prefectural offices.
弘贄/宏贄 is Hongzhi (贄 = zhì). 殿直 is the office Dianzhi, not a generic Palace Guard.
